Requirement: The system shall provide an extensible GUI toolbox for visual inspection (VI) postprocessing.
Rationale / Notes: Primary business objective as stated by stakeholder.

Requirement: The system shall be evaluated against usability and stability KPIs.
Rationale / Notes: Success criteria defined by stakeholder.

Requirement: The primary user groups are trained employees and students (non-scientists).
Rationale / Notes: Impacts UI complexity and documentation level.

Requirement: The system shall eliminate manual labor by providing a centralized VI postprocessing toolbox.
Rationale / Notes: Core problem to solve.

Requirement: The tool is classified as operational (not strategic).
The system shall be designed for an expected lifecycle of 15 years.
Rationale / Notes: Impacts technology choices and maintainability requirements.

Requirement: The MVP shall include the host shell with the identification tool fully functional.
Rationale / Notes: Defines minimum viable product scope.

Requirement: The system shall follow internal standardization practices.
The system is not intended to become a company-wide platform.
Rationale / Notes: Limits scope of deployment and governance.

Requirement: The host shell shall use a docking-based window management model.
Rationale / Notes: Stakeholder preference over MDI or tab-based.

Requirement: The host shell shall prevent multiple instances of the same tool, except for basic/utility tools.
The GUI shall scale correctly on high-resolution displays.
Rationale / Notes: Users may have high-DPI monitors.

Requirement: The host shell shall provide a top-level tab bar with defined categories for tool navigation.
Tool search functionality is not required.
Rationale / Notes: Explicitly excluded by stakeholder.

Requirement: A quick access toolbar is not required.
Rationale / Notes: Explicitly excluded by stakeholder.

Requirement: The host shell shall persist the window/dock layout between sessions.
A unified notification system is not required.
Configuration shall be managed on a per-tool basis.
The application startup time shall not exceed 1 minute.
The application shall not exceed 32 GB of memory usage.
The host shell should attempt to isolate tool crashes so that one tool failure does not crash the entire application.
Rationale / Notes: Best effort, not mandatory.

Requirement: The system shall implement user role management based on Windows accounts.
New tools shall provide defined metadata for registration in the host shell.
Rationale / Notes: Metadata schema to be defined.

Requirement: The host shell architecture shall support easy integration of new tools without modifying core code.
Rationale / Notes: Core design requirement from thesis scope.

Requirement: Inter-tool communication, if implemented, shall be limited to basic data exchange (e.g., JSON).
Rationale / Notes: Minimal or no inter-tool communication expected.

Requirement: The host shell shall provide a centralized logging system.
The application shall be distributed as a single executable.
The codebase shall follow a medium level of modularization.
Rationale / Notes: Balance between simplicity and extensibility.

Requirement: The application shall be named "VI - Toolbox".
The host shell shall include the following base tools: Image Viewer, File Explorer, and Main Log viewer.
The primary programming language shall be Python.
Rationale / Notes: C++ may be used for performance-critical components.

Requirement: The GUI framework shall be Qt via PySide bindings.
Computer vision and OCR tasks should consider OpenCV and Tesseract as candidates, but the final technology selection shall be based on an evaluation of available OCR approaches.
Rationale / Notes: Stakeholder suggestion, not a hard constraint. Multiple OCR technologies exist and should be evaluated.

Requirement: The application shall run on Windows.
The codebase shall follow PEP 8 style guidelines.
Code documentation shall use NumPy/SciPy docstring format; design documentation shall use UML2.
Third-party dependencies shall be limited to GPL or LGPL licensed libraries.
Open-source dependencies shall be preferred over closed-source alternatives.
Python dependencies shall be sourced from the Python Package Index (PyPI).
Version control shall use Git hosted on the HHI GitLab server.
The branching strategy shall follow GitHub Flow.
The local build command shall be "nox -s build".
The developer run command shall be "python -m app".
The release run commands shall be "./app" or "python -m app".
Both Debug and Release build configurations should be supported (Release is mandatory, Debug is best-effort).
New developer setup shall not exceed: clone repo, create venv, one install command, run.
The test framework shall be pytest.
Unit tests shall be mandatory before merge or release.
Formatting and linting checks shall be enforced as basic quality gates.
The release artifact shall be a portable ZIP archive.
Releases shall be stored on a network share (minimum) or GitLab Releases (best case).
An optional GitLab CI configuration file shall be provided that mirrors local build commands.
The CI pipeline shall include stages for: build, unit tests, and artifact creation (ZIP).
A dependency lockfile strategy shall be used, prioritizing ease of use and maintenance.
The tool shall support JPG/JPEG and PNG image formats.
The tool shall handle images up to 20000×20000 pixels resolution.
Input images are expected to be in greyscale.
Rationale / Notes: Preprocessing assumption; may simplify CV pipeline.

Requirement: The tool shall support multiple identifier classes (human-readable text strings).
The tool shall support multiple font styles in identifier recognition.
Identifier formatting (character spacing, multiline layout) is not consistent across chips.
Rationale / Notes: Increases OCR difficulty; algorithm must be robust.

Requirement: Image batches shall be selected via folder selection.
The user shall manually select the Region of Interest (ROI) on the first image of the batch.
Rationale / Notes: ROI is applied to all images in the batch.

Requirement: If the first image is a bad example, the user shall be able to skip to the next image for ROI selection.
An acceptable OCR accuracy threshold shall be defined.
Rationale / Notes: To be determined during development/evaluation.

Requirement: Images with low OCR confidence shall not be renamed automatically.
The OCR algorithm shall handle image rotation within ±5 degrees.
OCR results shall be validated against a user-configurable regular expression defined in an editable config file.
The OCR engine does not need to be trainable on specific fonts or characters.
After the rename process, images with failed OCR shall be displayed with a zoomable image view and an editable text field for manual correction.
The user shall have the option to enable or disable a rename preview before starting the rename process.
Renamed files shall contain at least the recognized identifier; on OCR failure, the original filename shall be preserved.
Duplicate filenames shall be resolved by appending a numeric identifier.
Rollback of renaming operations is not required.
The identification tool shall log relevant metadata for each operation.
Rationale / Notes: Metadata details to be defined.

Requirement: Processing time per image shall not exceed 5 seconds (target: under 2 seconds).
Total batch duration shall not exceed N × 5 seconds (where N is the number of images).
The naming of the identification tool shall be defined.

The tool workflow shall follow this sequence: (1) Open tool in host shell, (2) Select image folder, (3) Configure settings (preview flag, regex flag, regex template), (4) Select ROI on zoomable image, (5) Start rename process, (6) Display failed recognitions with zoomable image and text field for manual correction.
Rationale / Notes: Complete end-to-end workflow as described by stakeholder.
